title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory on PyTorch PT2 file parsing code execution (ZDI-26-1056)
date_note: Coordinated public release date stated on the ZDI advisory.
summary: The Zero Day Initiative published advisory ZDI-26-1056 (CVE-2026-136429) for a flaw in how PyTorch parses PT2 files that exposes a dangerous function. ZDI says a remote attacker could run arbitrary code in the context of the current process, and that exploitation requires a user to open a malicious file. ZDI says the vendor rejected the report as expected behavior; the advisory names no patch.
plain: ZDI disclosed a flaw in how PyTorch opens PT2 files that could let an attacker run code if a user opens a malicious file. ZDI says the vendor called it expected behavior and the advisory names no patch.
exec: ZDI says opening a malicious PT2 file in PyTorch could allow code execution; the vendor rejected the report as expected behavior, per ZDI.
action: ZDI's only stated mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product; the advisory names no vendor patch.

validation.note: Only the ZDI advisory was read; it is the researcher's own primary page.

review.note: wording: dangerous method changed to ZDI's dangerous function; rest matches ZDI
